item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 112320
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located near the coast of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
A tropical wave over the far eastern part of the east Pacific is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions are expected to be conducive for gradual development, and
a tropical depression is expected to form well south of southern
Mexico by the middle or latter half of the week as the system moves
generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 18a
item.description:
Issued at 600 PM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 112353
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 18A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
600 PM CST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
...MAJOR HURRICANE SIMON PARALLELING WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
...BRINGING HEAVY RAINS AND STRONG WINDS TO THE COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 600 PM CST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.7N 105.8W
ABOUT 110 MI...175 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 50 MI...80 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...125 MPH...205 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...951 MB...28.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of El Roblito to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 600 PM CST (0000 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 19.7 North, longitude 105.8 West. Simon is moving 
toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h) and this general motion is 
expected to continue over the next couple of days with a gradual 
turn to the north and north-northeast on Tuesday into Wednesday. On 
the forecast track, Simon is expected to remain near the coast of 
west-central Mexico tonight before moving a little farther away 
on Monday. Simon is then forecast to turn back towards the coast of 
Mexico on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 125 mph (205 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Simon is a category 3 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional weakening is 
forecast but Simon is still expected to be a strong hurricane as it 
passes near the coast of west-central Mexico tonight. Simon is 
expected to remain a hurricane when it moves farther offshore  
on Monday and Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60
miles (95 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 951 mb (28.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely occuring in the Hurricane
Warning area, with hurricane conditions spreading northward later
this evening into Monday.
 
Hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area by
Wednesday, with tropical storm conditions possible by Tuesday night.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of
2 to 4 inches with isolated additional amounts of 8 inches over
portions of the states of Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Sinaloa
through early Thursday. Isolated maximum storm totals of 30 inches
are possible over portions of the states of Michoacan, Colima, and
Jalisco. This rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides or worsen any on-going flooding, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate
coast near and to the east of where the center approaches land. Near
the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and destructive
waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 112112 CCA
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  18...Corrected
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Sun Oct 11 2026

Corrected spelling of Sierra in first sentence.

Simon is still a Category 4 hurricane, but appears to be feeling the 
effects of the nearby high terrain of the Sierra Madre Mountains as 
the inner core is brushing up against the Mexican coast. The eye 
remains observed on geostationary satellite imagery, but is more 
cloud filled than earlier with warmer surrounding cloud tops. While 
the 18 UTC subjective Dvorak fix was still at T6.5/125 kt, the 
objective intensity estimates have continued to fall, with values 
now in the 109-115 kt range. Therefore, the initial intensity is 
being lowered to 115 kt for this advisory. An earlier Synthetic 
Aperture Radar (SAR) RCM-1 pass was very useful to adjust the 34- 
50- and 64-kt radii of Simon as the hurricanes wind field continues 
to shrink in size. 

Simon has stubbornly maintained a north-northwestward motion, 
roughly parallel to the coastline, estimated at 335/5 kt. It is now 
looking increasingly likely that Simon will avoid making a direct 
landfall in the short-term, though its eastern inner core will 
likely produce hurricane conditions as the storm continues to move 
north-northwestward from Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes this 
afternoon and evening. The steering ridge centered over the Texas 
coast is likely to maintain this motion now for the next several 
days, though with some slowdown in the motion due to a weaker but 
competing ridge located to Simon's southwest. On Tuesday into 
Wednesday, a large short-wave trough is forecast to move across the 
southwestern United States and this feature should provide enough 
southwesterly environmental flow to turn the hurricane to the 
northeast, finally reaching the coast of Mexico in 60-72 h. Compared 
to this morning, the guidance has shifted westward and slower once 
again, and there remain some outlier solutions like the GFS that 
want to turn Simon southwestward beyond 48 h. However, the majority 
of the ensemble guidance (European-EPS, Google DeepMind) do show 
this slow recurving solution back into Mexico. The NHC track 
forecast is a little bit west and slower for the first 36-48 h, but 
then bends back to the previous forecast track thereafter, still 
showing Simon moving inland and dissipating in the day 3-4 period.  
This forecast still remains low confidence. 

Intensity wise, it is now looking more likely that Simon will not 
weaken as much as originally expected, now that it is only brushing 
up against the coast instead of part of its inner core moving 
inland. Still, the high topography in Jalisco should still have a 
negative effect, which has already been seen in Simon's wind field 
shrinking in size. The hurricane-regional models still show 
significant weakening over the next 12-24 h, even the ones that only 
skirt the coast of Mexico, and the NHC intensity forecast still 
shows a fast rate of weakening during that time. However, other 
environmental conditions remain very favorable, as shear stays under 
10 kt, and sea-surface temperatures warm to 31-32 C as Simon passes 
north of Cabo Corrientes and enters waters that have been unaffected 
by recent tropical cyclones (Polo and Rachel). However, there will 
be a significant amount of nearby dry air and it remains to be seen 
how intact Simon's inner core will remain over the next 24 h of near 
land interaction. The latest NHC intensity forecast now shows Simon 
maintaining hurricane intensity, and this forecast could still be 
low if the inner core remains more robust than the hurricane 
regional models are forecasting. This forecast is now on the higher 
end of the intensity guidance aids, but is under the SHIPS guidance 
this cycle, and also remains low confidence. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are 
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a 
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to El Roblito. 
Residents should continue to shelter in a safe room to ride out the 
storm as the most significant hazards with Simon are now ongoing.

2. Simon is now expected to approach the coast of west Mexico later 
this week, where Hurricane conditions are now possible along the 
coast of El Roblito to Bahia Tempehuaya. A Hurricane Watch is now in 
effect for this region. 

3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days. This 
rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico over the next few days. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  12/1800Z 21.0N 106.6W   80 KT  90 MPH
